dedupe_keys.name: em dat the international disaster database

description: EM-DAT holds records of the occurrence and impacts of more than 27,000 mass disasters worldwide from 1900 to the present, covering natural hazards (geophysical, meteorological, hydrological, climatological, biological, extra-terrestrial) and technological disasters. It is compiled and maintained by the Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED) at UCLouvain from UN agencies, NGOs, reinsurers, research institutes and the press, to support humanitarian action, disaster preparedness and risk reduction. An event enters when it meets thresholds such as deaths, people affected or a request for international assistance. Each record gives the hazard classification, country and subnational location, dates, magnitude, deaths, injured, affected, homeless and damage estimates, including insured losses and reconstruction costs. The living public table is updated weekly and downloaded as an Excel file from public.emdat.be after registration; non-commercial use is free under the terms of use, commercial use needs a paid annual licence. A validated archive is deposited on the UCLouvain Dataverse under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and yearly country profiles are on HDX. Caveats: reporting before about 1990 is incomplete, economic losses are often missing, small events fall below the thresholds, and infrastructure damage is not broken down by asset. Uses are calibration of hazard exposure and loss models, historical event analysis, resilience and climate adaptation studies. It complements DesInventar Sendai, which records smaller local losses, and GDACS for current events.
